newsitem.title: NORWAY: Ruhrgas more prepared for competition than BritGas.
newsitem.headline: Ruhrgas more prepared for competition than BritGas.

text.p: Ruhrgas, Germany's biggest gas company, will not suffer the same fate as its U.K. counterpart British Gas Plc despite an increasingly competitive German gas market, Burckhard Bergmann, vice-chairman of the executive board of Ruhrgas, said on Wednesday.

The introduction of competition in the U.K. gas market left British Gas with too much high-priced gas and too few customers, but Bergmann said Ruhrgas has protected itself against the threat of oversupply.
"We have a price review clause in all our (supply) contracts (with producers)...we can ask for a price adjustment if the competitive environment changes," Bergmann said.
Ruhrgas also has flexible supply contracts which allow the buyer to alter supply levels according to demand.
"In the 1980s, British Gas refused price clauses...but we (don't believe) we are intelligent enough to know the future 25 years ahead." Bergmann said.
Wingas, a joint venture between Russia's Gazprom and Wintershall, a unit of Germany's BASF AG, is Ruhrgas's main competitor in the German market.
Wingas already has a market share of five to six percent in the German market, which is set to increase to over 10 percent by the turn of century.
"Competition will increase but we are fighting," Bergmann said.

He added that Ruhrgas had covered most of its gas purchasing requirements for the next few years but could take additional small volumes from Norway and from the U.K. through the Interconnector pipeline.
